Which warn rules describe a condition that silently ruins a run and therefore belong at error?
Two skills declare no error rule at all: is that correct for them, or an oversight?

What is the exact test case that must flip for the exemption defect?
Which second rule rests on the same false premise?

Which of those are detectable from the command string alone, and what is the check predicate for each?
What pre-execution hook surface does Cursor actually expose in this repo?
Can a Cursor preflight adapter exist, and what is the smallest one reusing the shared library unchanged?
Can OpenCode's plugin API deny a Bash tool call before execution, and where is that stated?
What is the smallest OpenCode adapter, compared against what the audit file already collects?
Is every check named in a cli-* SKILL.md implemented, and is every registry check reachable?

What single CI guard would catch the drift class?
What do the four Hermes plugin prompt sections cost against the caps, and what headroom remains?
Is a repo-rules digest section worth the headroom versus naming the file in the dispatch prompt?
What would break in the repo if the section 7 heading emoji changed?

Which failure paths silently disable dispatch enforcement?

How does every recommendation rank by (failure severity x confidence) / cost?

keyFindings.text: NEW DEFECT: DISPATCH_SHAPES requires -p/--print after 'codex exec', which the real dispatch shape lacks; both documented codex commands produce NO-MATCH, so the codex preflight and audit are inert while HEADLESS_DISPATCH_SHAPES classifies the same command correctly.

stdin-redirect-required is declared warn in all seven cli-* skills while its violation is a silent hang with zero output; the check is deterministic from the command string across every headless shape, making the seven flips the highest-value severity change.

The false -s exemption is encoded in six artifact classes: the check clause and constant, the rule message (canonical + generated mirror), two test assertions, the upstream live-help row, the persona dispatch contract in a reference plus two playbook scenarios, and the dated benchmark reports.

The exact test that must flip: dispatch-rule-checks.test.mjs lines 118-119 asserting zero violations for -s cli-hermes and --skills=cli-hermes without --ignore-rules must become ['ignore-rules-required']; no second hard rule uses HERMES_SKILL_PRELOAD, so the registry enforcement site is singular and the persona dispatch contract is the second dependent.

hermes-explicit-toolsets-required does not require file; -t search,todo passes even though search is web-only and todo cannot read, so the leaf exits 0 with empty stdout. Requiring file in the parsed toolset list is the minimum fix.
cli-claude-code (2 rules) and cli-opencode (5 rules) declare zero error rules; both are oversights, and neither carries an availability rule while five sibling skills do.

explicit-model-required (429 retry loop, no output) and command-flag-for-slash-prompt (slash text delivered as prose) both produce silent wrong results and belong at error; no-bare-agent-general errors loudly and stays warn with a predicate fix.
Pi's --offline flag is mandatory in the fan-out builder (without it a non-interactive run hangs minutes on startup network probes) but no hard rule declares it and no check implements it.

Twelve check predicates are specified for the unenforced silent classes: hermes read-toolset/provider/source/no-z/budget, pi offline/provider-qualified-model, opencode dir, cursor model-pinned, claude/codex model-pinned, devin permission-mode advisory.
Budget-shorter-than-work is decidable only when both numbers co-appear; the predicate compares --run-budget against a timeout wrapper minus the 60s margin the builder already uses.

Cursor exposes a live preToolUse surface with matchers in .cursor/hooks.json; three adapters already run there, including a Shell-matcher git advisory built on the shared hard-rule engine. The dispatch gap is wiring, not platform.

The smallest Cursor dispatch preflight is a translation shim over the Claude adapter, exactly as task-dispatch-guard.mjs already translates Claude envelopes to Cursor's {permission:'deny', user_message, agent_message} + exit 2 or {permission:'allow', agent_message}.

OpenCode denies pre-execution by throwing from tool.execute.before; the plugins README names the throw as the deny signal and the deep-loop guard implements it with a prefixed error. The advisory channel is buffer-and-drain on experimental.chat.system.transform.

The smallest OpenCode dispatch preflight adds tool.execute.before to the existing audit plugin; imports and project-dir resolution are already present, no subprocess is needed, and the dispatch kill-switch ordering (check first) is inherited.

The declared-check/implemented-check bijection holds exactly (17/17) in both directions today and was verified by running the parser and registry, not by reading. The existing CI guard covers declared-to-implemented only.

Realized drift: two dispatch-shape registries (codex divergence), four model rosters duplicated as literals between executor-config.ts and fanout-run.cjs, README documenting 5 of 17 checks, and a 'four availability rules' comment above five.

One table-driven guard catches the drift class: shape parity across both registries over one documented command per runtime, bijection both directions, roster agreement, and per-check pass+violation fixtures.

Measured prompt-section costs against the 4000-char per-section cap: session-context 303 without / 3402 with a bound packet (headroom 3697/598), persona 276-321 fixed, goal 0 to 3621 worst case (headroom 4000/379), advisories variable; no enforced total cap exists.

A repo-rules digest section is not worth the headroom: 4000 chars carries 16% of the 25,085-char AGENTS.md, over-cap sections are skipped (not truncated), and it would be a fifth ungoverned copy; naming the file in the dispatch prompt costs one line.

AGENTS.md carries exactly one U+200D at line 247 (teacher sequence); changing it breaks no automated check: emoji enforcement is removed from sk-doc, SECTION_EMOJIS does not police H2s, the Gate 1 pointer generator extracts a single marker line, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink.

NEW DEFECT: the runner wires HERMES_SPEC_FOLDER and SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY but never HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS=1; the packet states that without it (and a plugins.enabled line) a Hermes dispatch runs with no repo guard hooks, so both wired markers are inert.

HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA is never set (confirmed fact); the plugin persona section reads only that env, so the section renders empty; the native-shaped fix is persona env plus -s agent-<name>, sequenced after the exemption fix.

Claude and OpenCode builders lack the availability probe the other five implement; codex default o4-mini and opencode default anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 diverge from the packet defaults; codex service tier defaults only when provided.

Twelve disablement paths; nine are invisible at runtime (missing skill file, parse failure, throwing check, unregistered hook, moved adapter, persisted kill switch, shape no-match, broken Pi symlink, wiring env gap). Cheapest detector bundle: one static CI wiring+fixtures test, one session-start kill-switch line, builder units plus one live lineage.
Only Codex is reconciled via install-codex-hooks --check; nothing asserts the Claude/Cursor/Devin configs still carry the preflight entry, and Devin's dispatch entry has no mkHookDrift fallback.

Do-now: codex shape, Hermes plugin opt-in, exemption removal, hermes file-toolset, stdin flips x7, opencode flips, AGENTS joiner. Do-next: CI guard, OpenCode before-hook, Cursor shim, pi checks, predicate fixes and additions, builder parity, Devin fallback, mcp severity, kill-switch advisory, persona wiring, permission-mode redesign, doc sweep. Do-not: digest section, per-dispatch self-test, roster copy, engine reimplementation, generated-artifact edits, fail-closed.

Phases: (1) close the four silent holes (no deps), (2) extend coverage (after 1), (3) wire the builders (persona after 1), (4) make silence loud (after 1 and 3), each with a runnable closing gate the operator can scaffold from.

ruledOutDirections: Flipping every warn rule to error irrespective of failure class
Editing the generated .hermes mirror or the dated benchmark reports
Treating Cursor or OpenCode as lacking a pre-execution surface
Adding a repo-rules digest prompt section
A third model-roster copy inside the hook engine
Per-runtime reimplementations of the shared hard-rule engine
